answer: Make every agent stake something scarce that is hard to mass-produce: a deposit of funds or compute locked in escrow, plus a reputation earned only through verified completed work. To forge one credible identity is cheap, but forging thousands is ruinous, because each needs its own stake and its own earned history. Like copper wiring, the cost scales linearly with every new identity while fraud payoffs stay flat. Pair that with cipher-based attestation: each agent's work is signed with a key tied to its stake, so peers can audit the chain and spot clusters of identities sharing one operator.
